name: Rio de Janeiro
title: Holidays in Rio de Janeiro
intro: Christmas in summer on Copacabana beach, a cable car up Sugarloaf Mountain and the world's biggest New Year's Eve party. Here's what Rio is like, when to go and how long to stay.
facts_note: Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: April to September is drier and milder. December to March is summer, hot and humid with afternoon storms, and Christmas, New Year and Carnival are the busiest and dearest times to go.

things.name: Christ the Redeemer
things.blurb: Ride the little train up through the forest to the famous statue on Corcovado.

things.name: Sugarloaf Mountain
things.blurb: Two cable cars climb to the top of the granite peak for views over the city and beaches.

things.name: Copacabana and Ipanema
things.blurb: Long, lively beaches with snack sellers, beach football and lifeguards.

things.name: New Year's Eve at Copacabana
things.blurb: Millions of people dressed in white watch fireworks over the beach at midnight.

things.name: Tijuca Forest
things.blurb: A huge rainforest in the city, with waterfalls, monkeys and trails.

things.name: Museum of Tomorrow
things.blurb: A striking science museum by the harbour, with hands-on exhibits about the planet.

faqs.question: Is Rio good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: It can be, especially with older children. Stay in a well-known area like Copacabana, Ipanema or Leblon and use registered taxis or ride apps.

faqs.question: Is Christmas a good time to go?
faqs.answer: It's summer, so the beaches are lively but it's hot and humid, with storms some afternoons. It's also the busiest time of year.

faqs.question: Is Rio safe?
faqs.answer: Crime is a problem in parts of the city, so check GOV.UK advice, keep valuables out of sight and go with a guide to less touristy areas.

faqs.question: How long is the flight?
faqs.answer: About 11 to 12 hours direct from London.
